I: What does good collaboration mean to you, fundamentally?

B: For me, good collaboration starts with listening. When people feel their perspective is genuinely received, a different kind of commitment appears. Without that listening, any method is just technique.

I: And how do you notice when something is not working?

B: Usually from the mood in the room. When it goes very quiet or everyone just nods along, that is a warning sign. Real participation is sometimes uncomfortable, and a bit of friction is part of it.

I: Has your attitude toward this changed over time?

B: Yes, clearly. I used to want quick results. Now I know that trust takes time and that a good process often matters more than a fast outcome. Patience is not a weakness, it is a precondition.

I: What would you advise someone new to these processes?

B: Not to act as if they already had all the answers. Keep questions open, tolerate disagreement, and regularly question your own role. Anyone who takes that seriously is rarely disappointed.
